parts.from: s28fp-1905-b2 p1 (main, brick): the sheet's BARN, its own outline from the north wall to the party wall at the trace's notch (sheet px y 4276-4285), walls at the trace's lines (T-1936)
s28fp-1905-b2 p1 (main, brick): the sheet's separate two-storey building south of the barn's party wall, its west wall 0.9 m in from the barn's (T-1936)

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s28fp-1905-b2 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 81% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed). T-1936: the plan is no longer the rules' fit. The sheet (sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_28.jpg, px x 2905-3110, y 3760-4495) draws two outlines here: the BARN, '2', from the north wall to a party wall at y 4280 (trace notches at y 4276-4285), and a separate '2' building south of it whose west wall stands about 0.9 m east of the barn's. The rules' one 7.75 by 36.5 m rectangle had been held inside the trace's label ticks; r1 and r2 now stand on the trace's own wall lines (r1 u -0.95 to 8.85, v 0.3 to 26.1; r2 u -0.95 to 7.9, v 26.1 to 36.5). Inferred: the outline is the sheet's, the split is the sheet's party wall, and both pictures that show the barn put its south corner within 0.6-1.7 m of that wall (reference views chicagology_923_photo, pictorial_1893_plate).

draft_elevation.note: T-1936, from the 1870s photograph of the Field house (a19-cgy-1905-field-923; source chicagology_1905_field_photo), whose right edge (x about 1595-2000 px) shows the barn's west (yard) face from v about 17.5 m to its south corner and the west part of its south end, read through the house's solved camera carried into this frame (reference view chicagology_923_photo) at about 36 px a metre on the face, every height from the camera's grade. READ FROM THE PHOTOGRAPH (the tier stays reconstructed: this attribute still carries the rules' choices for every face no picture shows): r1, the sheet's BARN, is ONE brick storey to a cornice whose top is 4.25 m up, with a mansard as its second storey (the sheet's '2'): the lower face to a curb about 7.4 m (lower_m 3.2), the deck the rules' 18-degree hip; the cornice 0.8 m deep on small brackets about every 1.2 m (y 938-951 px), over a pale stone frieze 2.6-3.1 m (y 953-970); four small windows 0.7 by 0.84 m with sills at 1.72 m at v 18.1, 20.5, 21.5 and 24.0 (x 1611-1815 px); three small pedimented dormers on the west face at v 17.6, 21.1 and 24.6 and one in the middle of the south end; a square louvred ventilator about 3.2 m across on the ridge at v 17.3 (x 1617-1747 px), four panels a face, its drum to about 9.3 m under a pyramidal cap to 10.5 m and a finial; three stacks and two spirelets on the roof (x 1722-1992 px). The 1893 plate shows the same cornice, frieze, mansard and dormers. STILL THE RULES' OR INVENTED: the face's north 17 m, behind the house in every picture, carries five more windows at a 3 m rhythm and four more dormers at the photograph's 3.5 m pitch; the alley face and north end take the rules' openings, the photograph's dormers mirrored and the cornice, brackets and frieze carried round; the stacks' places across the roof (one view gives their x, not their depth); the colours (the pictures are monochrome: red brick per the sheet, slate); and r2, the sheet's south building, the rules' two flat-roofed storeys. Liberty L-t1936-field-coach-house; the draft's L-draft-prairie-18-20-east-2330 no longer covers this record.

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '2-storey brick BARN on the alley'. 1911 labels it a garage or barn; for 1904 the envelope is backcast and its use reconstructed as a stable/coach house. The period description puts Field's "stables and other out-buildings ... in the rear, on the side nearest the lake".

A construction date for any building it draws

Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2330, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1936 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 28 trace (s28fp-1905-b2), the T-1841 census (s28-1905-rear) and the T-1837 register row frontage-28-055; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-18-20-east-2330). T-1936 refines it from the pictures that show it: the 1870s photograph of the Field house (a19-cgy-1905-field-923, source chicagology_1905_field_photo), whose right edge shows the south 9 m of the barn's yard face and the west part of its south end past the house's rear, read through the house's own solved camera (T-3271) carried into this frame; the 1893 Pictorial plate and the 1893 engraving, which show the same mansard; and the Daily News negative DN-0003324, c. 1905, which shows its snow-covered mansard and dormers behind the conservatory. The 1911 sheet draws two outlines here, the BARN and a separate two-storey building south of its party wall; the pictures show the barn alone, so the south building dates from 1893-1911 (liberty L-t1936-field-coach-house).
